To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the functional performance of long-term survivors with cGV HD is substantially below that of the US normative population, and that impaired functional performance is associated with cGV HD symptom burden, functional capacity, and the intensity of systemic immunosuppressive therapy.

functional performance is impaired in survivors of allogenic HCT with cGVHD; the most severe decrements in physical functioning were observed in physical function and role physical; six factors explained 56% variance in functional performance; intensive systemic immunosuppresion, reduced capacity for amubulation, and greater symptom bother were significant independent predictors of impaired functional performance; and symptom bother had a direct and indirect effect on functional performance.

functional performance in long term survivors of allogenic hematopoietic cell transplantation with chronic GVHD (cGVHD) is significantly lower than the normative US population and is associated with time since cGV HD diagnosis, cGV HD severity, intensity of systemic immunosuppressive therapy, comorbidity status, functional capacity, and cGVHD symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of cGVHD and its treatment on functional performance.
the impact of chronic graft-versus host disease (GVHD) on functional performance, defined as the ability to perform physical activities in daily life.
the development, evaluation and implementation of interventions that promote health and enhance the well being of individuals with chronic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important factors affecting the functional performance in patients with cGVHD after hematopoietic SCT are cGVHD symptom severity and intensity of immunosuppresion.
the functional performance of patients with cGVHD is impaired and that there are several factors that can account for the functional limitations.
chronic GVHD is the main determinant of functional performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cGVHD has a significant effect on the functional status of patients.
cGVHD has significant effects on the quality of life and the functional performance of patients who have undergone allogeneic stem cell transplant.
functional performance is impaired in survivors of allogenic hematopoietic cell transplantation with cGVHD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single cause for impaired functional performance in this population.

the physical function and role function of long-term survivors of hematopoietic cell transplant with chronic graft-vers-us-host disease is substantially lower than the general US population and that this impairment is not accounted for by age, gender, time since diagnosis, or comorbidity.
there are many different ways to approach this question.
